title: Investigate KV-prefix warmpath semantic changes during model swap and config toggles
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Background:
Teams have reported intermittent semantic changes in generated outputs when requests hit the KV/prefix cache after model variant switches or when we toggle quantization/batching settings. These changes are subtle: surface tokens may be identical for short prompts but downstream answers change semantics (e.g., numeric rounding, list ordering, or factual rearrangement). This ticket investigates the warmpath behavior of the KV/prefix cache across configuration and model/version transitions, builds a reproducible eval harness, and defines gating for rollouts.

Scope and goals:
- Reproduce deterministically (or probabilistically with confidence intervals) the class of cache-hit-induced semantic deltas observed in customer reports.
- Instrument the runtime to capture full input pairs (original request + cached hit variant), KV signatures, model-version and kernel-selection metadata.
- Build an eval suite that compares outputs for paired runs: cold (no cache hit) vs warm (cached state applied) across model swaps and config toggles (quantization level, batch size, kernel selector).
- Quantify regressions using multiple metrics (token-level diff rate, normalized edit distance, semantic similarity via embedding cosine, and downstream task-specific metrics where applicable).
- Propose rollback or mitigation strategies (strict prefix invalidation on model swap, versioned cache keys, conservative warmpath gating).

Hypotheses to test:
1) Cache key namespace collisions across model variants cause incorrect prefixes to be applied when model IDs are aliased (misrouting).
2) Kernel selection or quantization fallback changes the numerical rounding of KV values leading to diverging attention context in long-tail prompts.
3) Asynchronous prefetch/warm path may materialize stale KV entries during fast model rollouts, creating transient but customer-visible drift.

Planned experiments and harness design:
- Paired A/B runner that sends identical traffic and captures: request id, model id, model checksum, config blob, KV-sig, raw KV bytes (hash), output text, logits snapshot (where feasible), and embeddings.
- Datasets: production-sampled prompt seeds (anonymized), targeted adversarial prompts designed to expose key collisions (synthetic prefixes), and domain-specific prompts (math, instruction-following, code).
- Metrics: percent output token delta, BLEU/ROUGE for structured outputs, embedding cosine similarity threshold, and a semantic-change classifier flag (trained from historical regressions).
- Statistical gating: require 95% CI on observed delta rates with p-value threshold for flagging regression.

Deliverables:
- Eval harness repository link and CI job that runs on each model or config change PR.
- Dashboard tiles in Console showing paired-corpus delta rates per model, per config, and time-series around rollouts.
- Runbook for rollback and cache invalidation knobs to apply during rollouts.

Risks and non-goals:
- We will not address unrelated model quality regressions (e.g., prompt-tuning model drift) unless clearly correlated with cache hit metadata.
- Full logits capture may be limited by privacy and size; sampling and hashing strategies will be used.

Why this matters:
Subtle semantic regressions undermine trust in rollouts and auto-fallbacks. Because the KV/prefix cache is a strong cost and latency optimization, we need robust defenses to ensure cache hits do not change semantics when operators change model variants or runtime config.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Repro: At least one deterministic or statistically significant reproduction of a reported semantic change for a real prompt cluster.
2) Harness: A repeatable CI job that runs paired cold/warm tests on PRs touching runtime, routing, or model-variant metadata.
3) Metrics: Console dashboard that surfaces per-model paired-delta rates and an alert if delta exceeds threshold (default: token-diff-rate > 0.1% and embedding similarity drop > 0.02).
4) Mitigations: A documented rollback and prefix-invalidation procedure with automation (scripts) that can be executed in < 30 minutes.
tasks: Design paired-run harness and data schema for cold vs warm comparisons
Add runtime instrumentation: KV-sig, model checksum, kernel selector to request trace
Assemble anonymized sample prompt corpus from production (privacy review required)
Implement evaluator metrics: token-diff, edit-distance, embedding cosine, semantic-change classifier
Run controlled model-swap experiments across two models and three quantization configs
Create Console dashboard and CI job to run harness on each model/config PR
Draft rollback runbook and add an automated cache-invalidation endpoint
Share findings with runtime, model onboarding, and platform teams; propose gating rules
